security_spec.violation_condition: OpenSBI writes mseccfg.MML=1 or mseccfg.MMWP=1 (which lock those fields until reset) before all PMP entries are programmed to match the MML=1 truth table encoding — specifically, OpenSBI must ensure M-mode code/data regions use the correct A/L field values (L=0,X=1,W=1,R=0 for shared-code regions accessible to lower modes but with M-mode execute) and that no unlocked PMP entry inadvertently grants M-mode unrestricted access to S/U-mode memory. Once locked, a misconfigured PMP entry is irreversible and permanently breaks the expected protection boundaries.
security_spec.vulnerability_pattern: CSR write to mseccfg with MML or MMWP set (CSRW/CSRS mseccfg, imm) that is not immediately preceded by a complete PMP entry setup loop writing all pmpcfg/pmpaddr CSRs and followed by a read-back validation fence (no re-check of pmpcfg values after mseccfg write)
security_spec.summary: ePMP mseccfg fields are write-1-to-lock; OpenSBI must fully configure PMP entries for MML=1 semantics BEFORE setting MML/MMWP, else the locked misconfiguration creates an irreversible privilege-escapable memory protection gap
